signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Intervention + Options
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.45, collapsing through its SMA20 (162.61) and SMA50 (161.33) anchors following suspected BoJ intervention and a hawkish Fed hold. JPY is the week's G10 leader with a +1.683% average return, while USD is the laggard at -1.391%, creating a massive 3.074% bilateral spread. Despite the 275bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry advantage for USD, the options market is aggressively positioned for JPY strength, evidenced by a -1.38 25d risk reversal (Saxo) and a negative -1.7% Vol Risk Premium (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.9%). Speculative positioning remains heavily net short JPY at -114,030 contracts (COT), suggesting the current move is fueled by a rapid, disorderly unwind of the carry trade. Price is now testing the SMA200 at 157.89 as the next major structural floor. Risk: BoJ fails to follow up with policy normalization at the July 31 meeting, allowing carry-seekers to re-establish shorts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — BoE Hawkish Hold + Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3463 after BoE Governor Bailey signaled that upside rate risks remain built into market pricing despite a slow softening in the labor market. The pair has cleared its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3381/1.3364/1.3398), shifting the technical bias to bullish. The options market reflects acute hedging demand with a +3.9% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 7.1%), indicating traders are paying a significant premium for protection following the hawkish hold. Speculators are already net long +33,812 contracts, aligning with the positive Economic Surprise Index of +5.5. While the SOFR-SONIA OIS spread is nearly flat at -8bp, the real rate differential favors GBP at -0.13% vs USD +1.51% on an expectations-adjusted basis. Risk: Bailey pivots to a more balanced tone in upcoming speeches if disinflation accelerates.

signals.title: AUD/USD — ESI Divergence + Carry vs Options Skew
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7024, holding above its SMA50 (0.7017) despite a strong negative Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of -16.7. The pair is supported by a significant +70bp AONIA-SOFR carry advantage and a restrictive -1.15% real rate, which keeps the RBA hike bias intact for the August 11 meeting. However, the options market displays caution with a -0.72 25d risk reversal and an extreme +6.3% Vol Risk Premium (IV 12.4% vs HV30 6.1%), suggesting institutional players are hedging against a downside break. COT data shows speculators are currently net long +20,521 contracts, but the persistent data misses in the ESI pose a threat to this positioning. A sustained close below 0.7017 would invalidate the immediate bullish setup. Risk: RBA shifts to a neutral bias at the next meeting due to the persistent ESI misses.

signals.title: EUR/CHF — Retail Sentiment Extreme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: EUR/CHF trades at 0.9281, facing pressure as the Swiss Economic Surprise Index (ESI) hits a strong positive extreme of +35.6 vs the Euro's +9.3. Retail sentiment has reached an extreme 87% short position (Myfxbook), providing a contrarian signal for a reversal higher if CHF safe-haven demand cools. While the ECB-SNB nominal spread offers a +240bp carry advantage for the Euro, the real rate differential is narrow (EUR +0.12% vs CHF -0.03%), limiting the structural upside for the cross. Technicals show USD/CHF holding above its SMA cluster (0.8020/0.8103), suggesting broad CHF strength is currently contained despite the data outperformance. Risk: A spike in the VIX above 25 triggers acute safe-haven CHF bids, overwhelming the retail contrarian signal.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Correlation Break + OIS Carry
signals.text: USD/CAD is trading at 1.4001, remaining pinned near parity despite a significant correlation break with WTI Oil (corr -0.908 vs norm -0.024, z=-1.54σ). This decoupling suggests that the 150bp SOFR-CORRA carry advantage is currently a more dominant driver than energy prices for the Loonie. Speculative positioning is heavily net short CAD at -99,823 contracts (COT), making the pair vulnerable to a squeeze if Canadian data begins to outperform its neutral ESI of +4.0. Price is currently holding above the SMA50 (1.4041) on a daily basis, but intraday action shows a move toward the 1.4000 psychological level. Risk: WTI Oil breaks above $88, forcing a re-correlation and a CAD short-squeeze.
